passage_parts.label: A
passage_parts.title: A Chef's Story
passage_parts.text: People call me a zongpushi, a master chef for roadside banquets. Last Saturday, my team cooked a wedding feast for a family in our town. Our work started the day before. My helpers put up a big tent over the road, set out round red tables, and built an outdoor kitchen next to them. Then we washed and cut vegetables for hours. In the old days, there were no refrigerators. Chefs like my grandfather made sausages and fish balls at the host's home the day before, and they hung some of the food outside to dry. Someone had to guard it from hungry cats and dogs. On Saturday, we lit the stoves at four in the morning. As the master chef, I decide every dish and the order in which the dishes go out. My helpers are called water feet, because they work with water all day as they wash, cut, and serve.

passage_parts.label: B
passage_parts.title: From a Guest's Blog
passage_parts.text: Yesterday I went to my cousin's wedding banquet, and it was held right on our street! Under the tent, ten of us shared a round table. The first plate was cold, with sliced meat and jellyfish, so it did not matter that my uncle arrived late. Then the hot dishes kept coming: thick soup, steamed fish, and crab on sticky rice. My favorite was Buddha Jumps Over the Wall, a rich soup with many treasures inside. In the middle of the meal, the parents of the bride and groom walked from table to table to raise a toast. We finished with chicken soup, sweets, and fresh fruit. The whole meal took about two hours. Before I left, the helpers were already stacking chairs and clearing the tables. Grandma packed some leftovers to take home. She told me that in her village, leftovers used to be cooked into one big pot of soup for the neighbors who had helped.

questions.stem: What are the two texts mainly about?

options.A: Roadside wedding banquets, as seen by a chef and by a guest.
options.B: How refrigerators changed the way chefs keep their food.
options.C: Why Buddha Jumps Over the Wall is a guest's favorite dish.
options.D: How young people today can train to become master chefs for banquets.

options.B: They lit the stoves early in the morning.
options.C: They set up a tent, tables, and a kitchen by the road.
options.D: They asked the neighbors to lend them bowls and stools.

questions.stem: In Text A, what does “it” refer to?

options.B: The food hung outside to dry.

options.B: Grandma had saved some leftovers for him.

1.explanation_zh: 文本 A 是總鋪師自述他的團隊上週六為一戶人家辦婚宴：前一天搭棚、擺桌、備料，當天清晨起灶。文本 B 是一位賓客的部落格，寫他在自家街上參加表哥（堂哥）婚宴的經過。兩篇寫的是同一類事件──一場路邊的婚宴辦桌，分別從廚師和客人的角度來寫。
evidence: Last Saturday, my team cooked a wedding feast for a family in our town.
Yesterday I went to my cousin's wedding banquet, and it was held right on our street!

option_notes_zh.B: 文本 A 只用一句話提到從前沒有冰箱（文中確實有 there were no refrigerators），用來說明以前的做法，不是兩篇的主旨。
option_notes_zh.C: 佛跳牆是文本 B 作者最喜歡的一道菜，只是文本 B 的一個細節，沒有涵蓋文本 A。
option_notes_zh.D: 兩篇都沒有談年輕人怎麼學習成為總鋪師。

B: In the old days, there were no refrigerators.

1.strategy_zh: 多文本的主旨要同時涵蓋兩篇：文本 A 是辦桌的廚師，文本 B 是參加辦桌的客人，兩篇都在寫一場路邊婚宴。
hints: 文本 A 是誰寫的？寫什麼場合？
文本 B 是誰寫的？參加了什麼？
選能同時說明兩篇的選項。

2.explanation_zh: 文本 A 說工作從前一天就開始：助手們在路上搭起大帳篷、擺好紅色圓桌，並在旁邊搭好戶外廚房，然後洗菜、切菜好幾個小時。
evidence: Our work started the day before.
My helpers put up a big tent over the road, set out round red tables, and built an outdoor kitchen next to them.

option_notes_zh.A: 原文確實有 made sausages and fish balls at the host's home the day before，但那是「以前」作者祖父那一代總鋪師的做法，不是這次團隊做的事。
option_notes_zh.B: 起灶是婚宴「當天」（星期六）清晨四點的事，不是前一天。
option_notes_zh.D: 文中沒有提到向鄰居借碗或板凳。

option_notes_zh.B: 原文確實有 packed some leftovers，但那是奶奶在散席時打包剩菜帶回家，不是替叔叔留菜。

translation_zh.text:
文本 A　一位總鋪師的故事
大家叫我總鋪師，也就是路邊辦桌的主廚。上週六，我的團隊為鎮上一戶人家辦了一場婚宴。我們的工作從前一天就開始了。助手們在路上搭起一頂大帳篷，擺好紅色圓桌，並在旁邊搭起戶外廚房。接著我們洗菜、切菜，一做就是好幾個小時。從前沒有冰箱。像我祖父那樣的總鋪師，會在前一天到主人家做香腸和魚丸，並把一部分食物掛在外面風乾。得有人看守，免得被飢餓的貓狗吃掉。星期六當天，我們清晨四點就起灶。身為總鋪師，每一道菜和上菜的順序都由我決定。我的助手被稱為「水腳」，因為他們洗菜、切菜、上菜，整天都在和水打交道。
文本 B　一位賓客的部落格
昨天我去參加表哥的婚宴，而且就辦在我們家那條街上！在帳篷下，我們十個人同坐一張圓桌。第一道是冷盤，有切片的肉和海蜇皮，所以叔叔晚到也沒關係。接著熱菜一道接一道上桌：羹湯、清蒸魚，還有紅蟳米糕。我最喜歡的是佛跳牆，一道料多味美的湯。用餐到一半，新郎和新娘的父母一桌一桌地敬酒。最後我們以雞湯、甜點和新鮮水果收尾。整頓飯大約吃了兩個小時。我離開前，助手們已經在疊椅子、收桌子了。奶奶打包了一些剩菜帶回家。她告訴我，在她的村子裡，以前會把剩菜煮成一大鍋湯，分給來幫忙的鄰居。
